stories.headline: South Korea's KOSPI crashes 9.99% as Samsung and SK Hynix shed over 12%, triggering circuit breaker

key_facts.fact: The KOSPI closed at 8,203.84 on Tuesday June 23, down 910.71 points or 9.99%, its biggest daily plunge since March 4 and the second-largest daily decline of the year.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kospi fell 9.99 percent to close at 8,203.84... The nearly 10 percent decline was the second-largest daily fall on the Kospi this year, after a 12.06 percent drop on March 4 following the outbreak of the Iran war.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the market's two largest stocks, slid 12.31% and 12.47% respectively, wiping out billions in market value.
key_facts.excerpt: The sell-off hit heavyweight chipmakers particularly hard, with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, the market's two largest stocks, sliding 12.31 percent and 12.47 percent, respectively.

key_facts.fact: The Korea Exchange activated a circuit breaker on the main board at around 2:33 p.m., halting trading for 20 minutes after the KOSPI fell more than 8% below the previous close; a sell-side sidecar had already been triggered at 11:40 a.m.
key_facts.excerpt: The Korea Exchange (KRX) triggered the measure at around 2:33 p.m. after the KOSPI plummeted more than 8 percent from the previous session's close... It marked the fourth time this year that the KRX has activated a circuit breaker.

key_facts.fact: The rout followed a tech-led sell-off on Wall Street where the Nasdaq sank more than 1% as Amazon, Nvidia and Microsoft fell sharply, with investors again questioning the AI-fuelled boom.
key_facts.excerpt: The rout followed a sharp drop on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq sank more than 1 per cent as market giants Amazon, Nvidia and Microsoft were sharply down.

key_facts.fact: Analysts attributed the drop largely to profit-taking in semiconductor stocks rather than a macroeconomic deterioration, a day after the index passed the historic 9,100-point level for the first time and the two chipmakers came to make up more than half the market's value.
key_facts.excerpt: The KOSPI has become increasingly dominated by the two chipmakers that now make up more than half of the market value, as they propelled the index past the historic 9,100-point level for the first time on Monday.

stories.headline: China's all-CPU LineShine dethrones El Capitan as world's fastest supercomputer at 2.198 exaflops

key_facts.fact: China's LineShine debuted atop the 67th TOP500 ranking, the first time a China-based system has led since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017, ending El Capitan's run at No. 1.
key_facts.excerpt: The debut of China's LineShine on the 67th edition of the TOP500 rankings ends El Capitan's run at the top the list and marks the first time a China-based system has led the rankings since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017.

key_facts.fact: Installed at the National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzhen, LineShine achieved 2.198 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack benchmark, more than 20% ahead of No. 2 El Capitan, and is the world's fifth exascale system.
key_facts.excerpt: LineShine achieved 2.198 exaflops on the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark, putting it more than 20% ahead of the No. 2-ranked El Capitan system at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

key_facts.fact: LineShine reached the top spot with a domestic CPU-only design built around China's LingKun platform, proprietary LingQi interconnect and Kylin OS, using nearly 14 million cores (LX2 304-core 1.55GHz processors, 13,789,440 total cores).
key_facts.excerpt: LineShine reached the top spot with a domestic CPU-only design built around China's LingKun platform, proprietary LingQi interconnect, and Kylin operating system.

key_facts.fact: It is the first supercomputer to officially exceed 2 exaflops on the Linpack benchmark; the announcement was made at the ISC26 conference in Hamburg, Germany.
key_facts.excerpt: The custom-built cluster composed of nearly 14 million ARM cores is the first to officially exceed 2 exaflops on TOP500's Linpack benchmark... unveiled today at ISC26 in Hamburg, Germany.

key_facts.fact: Experts said the result reflects Beijing's drive for self-sufficiency more than its AI standing: LineShine ranked only fourth on a benchmark designed to simulate AI-like work, and China had stopped submitting systems for three years amid US chip export controls.
key_facts.excerpt: the results may say more about Beijing's desire to show self-sufficiency in computing systems than its standing in the global AI race, experts said... LineShine ranked fourth on a benchmark test designed to simulate computing work that is more similar to AI.

stories.headline: Qualcomm in advanced talks to acquire AI infrastructure startup Modular at ~$4 billion valuation

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm is in advanced talks to acquire Modular Inc. in a transaction valuing the AI infrastructure software company at about $4 billion, per Bloomberg sources, with a deal possibly announced in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm Inc. is in advanced talks to acquire Modular Inc. in a transaction valuing the artificial intelligence infrastructure software company at about $4 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. A transaction may be announced as soon as the coming weeks.

key_facts.fact: The $4 billion valuation would mark a significant step-up from the $1.6 billion valuation Modular secured in a $250 million funding round just nine months ago, in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: If completed, the deal would mark a significant step-up from the $1.6 billion valuation Modular secured in a funding round just nine months ago... Modular has raised a total of $380 million to date, including a $250 million in a funding round in September.

key_facts.fact: Modular was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $380 million to date; Qualcomm is seeking to reduce reliance on the volatile handset market by branching into data center processors and autonomous vehicle chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2022, Modular has raised a total of $380 million to date... A global supplier of smartphone chips, Qualcomm has been working to reduce its reliance on the volatile handset market by branching out into fast-growing areas like data center processors and autonomous vehicle chips.

key_facts.fact: The Modular pursuit follows a separate reported Qualcomm deal to acquire AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8 billion to $10 billion, which would put combined commitments above $14 billion toward an AI data center ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that Qualcomm was also in late-stage talks to buy AI hardware startup Tenstorrent in a massive transaction valued between $8 billion and $10 billion... upwards of $14 billion in a matter weeks toward building a comprehensive AI data center ecosystem.

stories.headline: Groq raises $650M led by Disruptive and Infinitum to pivot into AI inference cloud after Nvidia deal

key_facts.fact: Groq announced $650 million in new growth capital on June 22, 2026, led by Disruptive and Infinitum, to accelerate expansion of its AI inference cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: San Francisco, CA, June 22, 2026 – Groq, Inc. today announced $650 million in new growth capital to accelerate the expansion of its AI inference cloud. The round was led by Disruptive and Infinitum, with participation from investors who elected to reinvest in the company.

key_facts.fact: Groq plans to scale toward 200 MW of capacity by the end of 2027, fitting out its existing 13 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East and APAC with Nvidia's new LPX system.
key_facts.excerpt: Already operating 13 data centers across North America, Europe, the Middle East and APAC... Groq expects to scale toward 200 MW by the end of 2027... the new LPX system from NVIDIA.

key_facts.fact: The raise follows Nvidia's December 2025 non-exclusive licensing deal for Groq's technology, in which Nvidia hired founder/CEO Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and others; Groq did not disclose its new valuation, having last been valued at $6.9 billion after a $750 million round in September.
key_facts.excerpt: The raise comes roughly six months after Nvidia signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement for Groq's technology and hired away founder and CEO Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra, and other employees. Groq did not disclose its new valuation. It was last valued at $6.9 billion following a $750 million round in September.

key_facts.fact: Groq's cloud platform now serves over five million developers and processes trillions of AI tokens each week, having pivoted from chips toward becoming an AI inference neocloud operator.
key_facts.excerpt: The company disclosed today that the platform is processing trillions of tokens per week for 5 million developers. Groq's cloud runs across 13 data centers spanning multiple continents.

stories.headline: SpaceX signs $6.3B compute deal giving Reflection AI access to Nvidia GB300s at Colossus 2

key_facts.fact: SpaceX signed a computing deal with open-source startup Reflection AI granting immediate access to Nvidia GB300 chips at the Colossus 2 data center, with Reflection paying $150 million per month from July 1, 2026 through 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Reflection will get immediate access to Nvidia GB300s... and has agreed to pay SpaceX $150 million per month beginning July 1, 2026, through 2029, according to materials viewed by CNBC.

key_facts.fact: The payments total about $6.3 billion if the agreement runs through the end of its term, though either company can end the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is worth up to $6.3 billion and either company has the option to end the contract with 90 days' notice after the first three months.

key_facts.fact: The Reflection deal is smaller than SpaceX's prior Colossus deals: Anthropic pays about $1.25 billion per month and Google $920 million per month, both also running through July 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is smaller than SpaceX's deals with Anthropic and Google, which cost the companies $1.25 billion per month and $920 million per month, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Reflection AI, last valued at $25 billion, is building American open-source AI models to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; the Colossus data center was originally built by xAI, now part of SpaceX, which has turned it into a commercial compute platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Reflection has leaned directly into that pitch as the startup, last valued at $25 billion, is trying to build American open-source AI models that can compete with frontier systems from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

stories.headline: Chevron and Microsoft sign 20-year deal for 2.67 GW gas-powered West Texas data center (Project Kilby)

key_facts.fact: Chevron announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to develop a co-located natural-gas power facility (Project Kilby) supplying dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center in West Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Chevron Corporation today announced that Energy Forge One LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary, has signed an agreement with Microsoft Corp. to develop a co-located power facility in West Texas that will provide dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center under a 20-year power purchase agreement.

key_facts.fact: Project Kilby is expected to deliver approximately 2.67 gigawatts of capacity, consuming roughly the power needed for about two million homes, making it among the largest co-located natural gas power and data center developments in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center, called Project Kilby, is expected to consume nearly 2.7 gigawatts of electricity, equivalent to the power needed to run about two million homes.

key_facts.fact: A majority of the generation will come from large GE Vernova turbines, with additional capacity from Solar Turbines, a Caterpillar subsidiary; the plant will have its own on-site power fueled by Chevron's Permian Basin natural gas in Reeves County.
key_facts.excerpt: Two large GE Vernova turbines will generate most of the power, with a Caterpillar subsidiary Solar Turbines providing the rest... Microsoft will buy power from the power plant for 20 years.

key_facts.fact: Chevron expects a final investment decision by the end of 2026 after acquiring necessary permits, with first power delivery anticipated in 2028; Microsoft said the multi-billion-dollar investment over five to seven years would support over 6,000 construction jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: The multi-billion-dollar data center investment, spanning the next five to seven years, is expected to support over 6,000 construction jobs... Project Kilby is expected to provide first power by 2028 and will ramp up to 2.67 gigawatts over time.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches Halos for Robotics, a full-stack safety system bringing AV-grade safety to humanoids

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced Halos for Robotics on June 22, 2026, described as the industry's first full-stack, open robotics safety system that extends Nvidia's autonomous-vehicle safety architecture to humanoids, industrial robots and autonomous mobile robots.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Halos for Robotics is the industry's only full-stack, open robotics safety system, extending NVIDIA Halos' proven autonomous vehicle safety to robotics and physical AI.

key_facts.fact: The platform pairs Nvidia IGX Thor hardware and Holoscan Sensor Bridge for AI compute with Halos OS (including Halos Core, a safety OS running Linux and QNX), leveraging over a decade of AV safety R&D, 18,000 engineering years and 21 billion safety transistors.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA launched the Halos for Robotics platform, integrating AI compute (IGX Thor) and a comprehensive safety OS (Halos OS), leveraging over a decade of AV safety R&D, including 18,000 engineering years and 21 billion safety transistors.

key_facts.fact: Agility Robotics is the first to use Halos for Robotics, integrating IGX Thor and Halos Core into the safe human-detection system of its humanoid Digit; Digit will be the first production robot shipping with Nvidia Halos OS, operating in warehouse environments alongside people.
key_facts.excerpt: Digit, Agility's humanoid, will be the first production robot shipping with NVIDIA Halos OS. It will operate in real warehouse environments, using NVIDIA IGX and Halos Core to safely navigate and work alongside people.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also opened the Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab, the world's first ANAB-accredited program for functional and AI safety in both autonomous vehicles and robotics, working with certification bodies including TÜV Rheinland, UL Solutions, TÜV SÜD, exida, SGS and CertX.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab is the world's first ANSI National Accreditation Board (ANAB)-accredited program for physical AI functional and AI safety, helping partners prepare Halos integrations for third-party certification by leading certification bodies including TÜV Rheinland, UL Solutions, TÜV SÜD, exida, SGS and CertX.
